## Findings: Plugin System and Dictate/Recite Integration

**Core/Plugin — what was built (2026-11-02/03):**

`public/framework/core/Plugin/` — `class Plugin extends Events(Object)`: one plugin system for the whole framework.

**UI settings offered:**
- **Live toggle on/off:** each plugin row has a checkbox; `Plugin.plugins` is a live List. Switching takes effect at once.
- **Config panel:** `static defaults` and `static fields` (key, label, kind) drive a generic config UI with text boxes, sliders, dropdowns. A plugin's row expands to show its fields when on.
- **Saved state:** `Plugin.store` (localStorage key: `plugin.<Host>.<Plugin>` = `{on, config}`). Only user changes through a row are saved.

**Shape of a plugin:**
```js
class BargeIn {
  static id = "barge"; static label = "Interrupt"; 
  static defaults = { on: true, mode: "volume" };
  static attach(instance) { /* setup */ }
  static detach(instance) { /* teardown */ }
}
Host.use(BargeIn);
```

**Paths:**
- Core: [core/Plugin/Plugin.js](/framework/core/Plugin/Plugin.js) · [core/Plugin/PluginEntry.js](/framework/core/Plugin/PluginEntry.js) · [core/Plugin/readme.md](/framework/core/Plugin/readme.md)

## Root cause of the mingled chat

**Confirmed culprit: `Servex/agents/Sessions.js:548` `assign_prompt()`, time-window merging, not Whisper chunking or edit redraws.**

A Prompt/message stays open and silently absorbs every new owner utterance while `s.prompt` is truthy — governed only by elapsed time (`prompt_close_ms`, default 8000ms, `Sessions.js:256,1273-1279`), not by whether the new sentence is actually a continuation. It closes early only when an assistant reply lands (`reply_closes_prompt`, `:1281-1286`).

**Live evidence** — `public/framework/ai/sessions/2026/11/03/v-z0jonhy/session.jsonl` lines 113–138: the owner said four distinct, unrelated sentences — *"In this technological form."* / *"You'll answer your question."* / *"Thank you."* / *"I don't answer your question."* — 0.2–5.5s apart. The smart seat was busy spawning the mastermind task and sent no reply in between, so nothing triggered an early close. All four got folded into one Prompt (`p-1793729237961`) and one message (`m-1793729237967`) via `PromptLines.push_raw`/`append_paragraph` (`sentences.push` at lines 121, 127, 136) — one card, four unrelated thoughts.

**The other hypotheses, checked and not supported here:**
- **Reply splitting an open bubble** — the code explicitly guards against this (`:1281-1285`, checks `this.thoughts.get(s.id)?.lines.length` before closing); no instance of it firing wrongly in this session.
- **Whisper chunk overlap/boundary** — every pushed text is a clean, complete, non-overlapping sentence; no raw Whisper log exists for this window (`public/framework/ai/whisper/bucket.jsonl` only holds an unrelated later run) to fully rule it out, but the clean boundaries argue against it.
- **`place`/improve edits reordering text** — each edit (lines 10, 32, 51, 71, 89, 101, 131, 139, 141, 144, 159, 167, 182, 199) retargets exactly one sentence id via `messages.clean`; never touches others.

**Smallest fix (not applied):** make the merge window close on a semantic boundary (sentence-ending punctuation + `floor:"done"`) rather than pure elapsed time, or shorten `SERVEX_SESSION_PROMPT_CLOSE_MS` so a slow smart-seat turn doesn't leave a multi-second absorption window open.

Full detail logged at `public/framework/ai/sessions/2026/11/03/session-f5eadae9/minion-mingled-chat/`.

## Reply path investigation — report

**(1) How a reply posts today**
- `Servex/agents/Sessions.js:1557-1620` `heard()` is the ONE place a turn's text becomes a reply. For the single-seat voice assistant: a pause cue (`s.cue_open`, set at `Sessions.js:722`) must be open when the turn ends, checked/cleared at `Sessions.js:1574-1577`; filler is dropped (`is_filler`). It then writes a plain `{"chat":{at, from:{kind:"assistant",id:"smart"}, via:"text", text, re}}` line (`Sessions.js:1608-1616`) straight to `session.jsonl` via `write()`.
- Browser: `ux/Dictate/Widget.js` `Thread.draw()` (`Widget.js:154-175`) reads **only** `entry.chat` and renders a bubble; `ext/Chat/v3` and `chat.js` read the same V1 `{chat}` shape. There's no SSE event name beyond the JSONL append itself — the session file append is the wire (`Follow`-style tail), not a bespoke event.

**(2) The item-tool path already exists in core, unused by Sessions.js**
- `Session.js:134` (`apply_line`) already handles `delta.messages` generically: `this.messages.set(delta.messages)`, which routes to `Chat` (a typed `List`, `core/Session/Chat/Chat.js`). `List.add()` (`List.js:277`) stamps ids and append order already.
- `Reply` (`core/Session/Chat/Reply.js`) is a ready-made typed member: `{re:{to:sentenceId}, level, text}`. So the smallest delta is literally `{"messages":{"add":{"type":"Reply","by":"smart","text":"…","re":{"to":"<sentence id>"}}}}` — handled today by `Session.apply_line` → `Chat.set` → `List.add`. **Nothing new needs building in core for the delta itself.**
- Gap: nobody writes it yet, and nothing in the UI reads `messages` deltas (Widget.js, Recite, v3 all read `chat`).

**(3) What adding it alongside the default would take**
- `Sessions.js`: in `heard()`, write both the existing `{chat}` line (unchanged, for V1) and a new `{"<prompt id>":{"messages":{"add":{...}}}}`-style delta — this is exactly the "dual-write, additive" plan already spec'd in `public/framework/core/Session/doc/one-replay-plan.md` ("Migration is additive... delta form written beside the old line... old lines stay until V1 is retired").
- Renderers: `Widget.js` `Thread.draw` needs a second branch for a `messages.add` entry, or V3 needs to read deltas directly (the doc's step 4, "V3 over the real classes" — not built).
- Read-aloud: `audio/Recite/Recite.js` `from_wire()` (`Recite.js:247-273`) reads only `line.chat`. If both paths write independently-renderable content, Recite would need a dedupe (read once, from whichever shape wins) — today it would simply **not** see a messages-only reply at all, so no double-read risk yet, but also no read-aloud for it without a Recite change.
- `cue_open`/drop-filler/echo: all keyed off the smart-seat text at turn-end in `heard()`; an item-tool call that fires mid-turn (before the result event) bypasses that gate entirely — it would need its own filler/cue check if meant to coexist with the default path, or be scoped to only fire when the agent explicitly chooses to (e.g., for a task-linked reply the plain-text path wouldn't otherwise produce).

**(4) Gains vs. costs**
- Gains: stable message id, explicit order, a `re`/task link, matches the owner's original item-tool model, is the documented target shape (V3).
- Costs: no streaming (today's chat is typed live via `live()`/delta text — a tool call is one shot, after the fact), extra tool round-trip latency per reply, and real double-posting risk if a future renderer draws both `chat` and `messages` for the same reply without a dedupe rule.

**(5) Why plain text originally** — `via:"text"` is in the very first voice-sessions commit (`e4ae149e6`, "Servex: voice sessions — fast+smart pair, Usage.pick"). It was the initial design, not a later shortcut, and I found no doc arguing against the item-tool path — only the still-unbuilt `one-replay-plan.md`, which the owner marked "not built."

**Recommendation / smallest first step:** don't touch `Sessions.js`'s gating logic yet. Ship `one-replay-plan.md` step 1 only: dual-write `{"<prompt>":{"messages":{"add":{type:"Reply",...}}}}` beside the existing `{chat}` line in `heard()`'s `smart` branch, with nothing reading it yet. That's reversible, additive, and gives a real delta stream to build a renderer against before deciding cue/Recite/dedupe semantics.

Findings logged to the task. Summary:

**Cause:** Not the item tool. `run_item_now` (`Servex/agents/page_tools.js:1147-1369`) always returns a plain object, and it's `JSON.stringify`'d (`page_tools.js:1439`) — the tool_result the model sees is always valid JSON, never literally `"undefined"`. `session.jsonl` around the task-add (lines 3452-3453) shows no `undefined` text written there; it's only the task-add line and the servex Ref line.

The real path is `single_cue()` (`Sessions.js:716-728`), which sends a bare `(pause)` nudge to the smart seat after the tool call. When that nudged turn ends, `heard()` (`Sessions.js:1565-1616`) takes `event.text ?? agent.last_text` and posts it as a chat bubble unless `is_filler()` (`Sessions.js:1726`) matches. `is_filler()` only screens known filler phrases and pure-punctuation — not the literal word `"undefined"`. So when the model's own text block for that nudged turn (right after a tool-only turn with no accompanying text) literally came back as the word `undefined`, it sailed through as a real reply.

**Smallest fix (not applied):** add a check in `is_filler()` for the trimmed, case-insensitive literal `"undefined"`/`"null"`, treated like `(listening)`. Answering the owner's direct question: yes, `is_filler` should drop that.

Now the final report to the parent, under 350 words.

**Found it — two different triggers, both already partly guarded, with the exact gap documented.**

**(1) 12:07:19 — true hallucination.** `bucket.jsonl` seq175: Whisper `final` returns `"Thank you."`, `no_speech_prob: 6.2e-11` (near zero — Whisper thought it heard real speech), `duration: 1.4s`, word prob for "Thank" only 0.14. `BargeIn.noise()` caught it and logged `"barge: phantom phrase dropped"` (seq176-177, `BargeIn.js:125`) — but that only stops Recite's own barge-in logic from reacting. The text had *already* been pushed into the owner's prompt stream (`session.jsonl:124`, `"fast"` writer) before the guard even ran.

**(2) 12:48:17 — echo, not silence.** seq992: Recite `"spoke"` at `18:48:13.266`, playing a 4.224s clip. seq995: Whisper `final` `"Thank you."` arrives at `18:48:15.503` — **2.24s into Recite's own TTS playback**, i.e. the mic picked up the assistant's own voice. `no_speech_prob` here is also near zero (`7.5e-9`) — real audio was present, just not the owner's. `Recite.echo_guard_ms` is 1500ms (`Recite.js:46`), so this landed just past the guard window, or the word-overlap `echo()` check (≥60% match against the sentence being read) simply didn't fuzzy-match "Thank you." against whatever Recite was actually saying.

**Why both got through to chat:** `audio/Recite/doc/architecture.md:29` already names this exact gap as an *open item, not built here*: every guard (`BargeIn.noise()`, `echo()`, near-silence) only stops Recite's barge-in/pause behavior — none of them gate `ux/Dictate`'s send path, which is what actually posts the owner's line to chat. It's filed as a task for `mastermind-ink-check` (owner of `ux/Dictate/`), not yet built.

**On the owner's specific questions:** `no_speech_prob` is exposed by whisper-server (seen in every `bucket.jsonl` line) but is *not* a reliable filter here — both phantom lines had near-zero `no_speech_prob`, since real sound (room noise or TTS leak) was present. A send-side filter needs: `BargeIn.noise(text)` (blocklist) OR `BargeIn.echo(text)` fuzzy-match while `Recite.echo_active()`, checked in `ux/Dictate`'s send path before posting — not a generic level/duration gate.

## Summary

Built "cutting in" for Recite/BargeIn on `worktree/qf-1` (commit `c6e064c07`):

- **`Recite.cancel_unheard()`** — stops playback and drops the *whole* queue (not just the reply playing), reporting each dropped reply through an injected `on_read({id, reply, chunk, sentence, heard: "cut"|"skipped", words})` callback.
- **`BargeIn.cut()`** replaces the old `heard_speech()` — on real owner speech (wire line or Whisper-confirmed volume trigger), calls `cancel_unheard()` by default; **`recite.resume_after_cut`** (default `false`, remembered) brings back the old pause-then-resume manners for whoever wants them.
- **Start grace** (`grace_ms`=1000) blocks the fast volume trigger right after a chunk starts, unless the owner was already talking — then **`quick_hold_ms`**=120 (not 250) cuts fast instead.
- **1 s minimum hold** before a fresh reply starts now applies whether or not the ear (`barge.on`) is on — `speaking()` no longer gates on it.

All touched tests pass headless against the worktree's own server (`qf-1.localhost`): `Recite.test.mjs`, `playback-stutter.test.mjs` (20/20, added 5 new), `ReciteBubble.test.mjs` (43/43). Updated `audio/Recite/readme.md` and `ux/Dictate/doc/echo-and-turn-taking.md`.

**Left undone** (noted in the task log): the local own-mic volume trigger doesn't yet fire while a reply is only *held* (`wait_at`, nothing playing) — only the wire-line path covers that; and `ext/Chat` isn't wired to post `on_read` as a `say` line (brief scoped this task to the client event + test, no Servex side).

Good, `group_start` exists and is used consistently. Review complete.

**Verdict: not ready to merge as-is from this pass — but no confirmed code defect found; the one apparent test failure is a stale test environment, not the diff.**

- **c6e064c07 (Recite/BargeIn cutting-in):** Logic read-through checks out — `cancel_unheard()` drops the whole queue (playing + pending), reports each once via `on_read` with dedup by `reply`, respects `resume_after_cut`; `grace_ms`/`quick_hold_ms` gating in `hear()` is correctly ordered before the hold-timer check. No `ext/Chat` import added to `audio/` — `on_read` is injected, direction is clean. `node --check` passes on all touched files. **However**, `playback-stutter.test.mjs` shows 4 failures (lines 125, 146–148) when run against `monorepo.localhost`. Root cause confirmed by `curl`: the live dev server is serving a **pre-change** `Recite.js` (has `heard_speech`, no `cancel_unheard`/`resume_after_cut` at all) — not this worktree's file. This is a server/proxy pointing issue, not a code defect; the server needs to be pointed at `worktrees/qf-1` (or restarted against it) before these tests mean anything. **Action before merge: re-run the test against the correct served copy** — I could not confirm the new behavior actually works end-to-end.
- `Recite.test.mjs` can't run in Node (needs DOM) — unchanged limitation, not new.

- **c8c0af7b2 (Plugin per-instance + re-attach):** `Plugin.test.mjs` 17/17 pass, including the two new tests for re-attach and per-instance toggle; asserts are real (checks specific counts/states, not just "no throw"). `enable()` now tracks every instance in `rec.live` unconditionally (previously only when `tracks`), kept past `disable()` — acceptable, WeakRef-pruned every 256. `PluginEntry.get_one`/`set_enabled`/`save_row` fallback logic for instance rows reads correctly.

- **Docs commits:** no code, nothing to test.

- **Stray files:** `public/public/...` duplicate tree exists but predates and is untouched by this branch — not this work's defect.

**Smallest fix:** none in the diff itself; fix the test environment (point `monorepo.localhost`'s served root at this worktree, or restart the dev server against it) and re-run `playback-stutter.test.mjs` before calling c6e064c07 verified.

**Merge: yes.**

- All three tests pass (`Sessions.single.test.mjs` 13/13, `phantom-gate.mjs` 7/7), `node --check` clean on all touched files, no stray untracked files.
- Whisper flags verified against the real binary's `--help`: `-mc N`/`--max-context` and `-sns`/`--suppress-nst` both exist; args array has each flag/value as a separate element (`Servex/Servex.js:505`) — syntactically correct.
- `should_drop_phantom` (`phantom-gate.js:25-37`) only fires on `BargeIn.noise()`-matched stock phrases, gated by echo-active OR short-clip OR low-word-prob — never blanket-drops an arbitrary "Thank you." (verified by the "normal length, Recite silent → kept" and "starts with Thank you → kept" fixtures). A separate `echo-match` branch (line 35) drops non-blocklisted text that fuzzy-matches what Recite is actively reading — reuses `BargeIn`'s own `echo()`, not a new blocklist, consistent with the law against duplicate lists.
- Wired correctly: `chat.js:201-210` calls the gate inside `deliver()`, before `Session.say()`, skipped for `via === "typed"`. A drop logs via `WhisperLog.event("composer", "dropped", …)` (line 207) and returns `true` (handled) instead of silently vanishing — satisfies "every drop is visible."
- `noise` is `BargeIn.noise`, a `static` method that never reads `this` (BargeIn.js:306) — safe to pass as a bare reference. `recite.barge.echo(text)` is called as a bound property access, not detached.
- Import direction: `chat.js` lives under `ux/Dictate`, not `ext/Chat` — the "ext/Chat must not import audio/" constraint doesn't apply here and isn't violated elsewhere in the diff.
- `is_filler` (`Sessions.js:1726`) now also matches a bare "undefined"/"null" string; the added test confirms a real sentence containing the word ("The value was undefined in the log.") is still kept.

## Fixes
1. **There's no `requirements.md` in the task folder.** The asks behind this diff only appear as cut-off spawn titles in `session.jsonl` and in the minions' own folders. A fresh agent couldn't tell from this folder what was asked or whether it was done.
2. **The new Whisper flags won't take effect the way the code says.** The comment at `Servex/Servex.js:507` says they apply after a Servex restart. But whisper-server runs detached, and on a restart Servex picks up the already-running process with its old flags (`Servex/Process.js:352`). The flags only apply once whisper-server itself is stopped and started again.

## What works
- **Hallucinated lines no longer post to the chat.** `chat.js`'s `deliver()` now runs BargeIn's existing checks before the line is sent, rather than a second blocklist. Typed lines are never checked, every dropped line is logged, and it's documented and linked from the Dictate readme.
- **A stray "undefined" or "null" reply is dropped**, with a test.

## Notes (smaller issues)
- **Stale Whisper info:** the gate keeps the last Whisper reply's details and never clears them, so a later sentence can be judged on an old clip.
- **Fragile hook-up:** the gate hooks into the mic by replacing its `on_whisper` handler, so anything that reassigns that handler cuts the gate off.
- **A real "Thank you." can vanish:** if said while a reply is being read aloud, or just after, it is dropped with no sign on screen.
- **The test has its own copy of the phrase list**, so it can't catch differences from the real list. For example, the real check doesn't trim spaces.
- **Stale comment:** the comment above `is_filler` in `Sessions.js` doesn't mention the new undefined/null case.

The diff changes no page layout, so I only answered the Requirements and Words sections and didn't use the three screenshots in the folder.
